brief: Goldman's Privorotsky says Monday's rebound followed one of the firm's most aggressive prime-book de-risking episodes in a decade. Thursday's momentum and high-beta unwind drove record low-volatility outperformance and took hedge fund net exposure to 5-year lows. He argues a bond rally on soft CPI could flip short-covering into a re-grossing cycle favoring aerospace, transports, discretionary and high-quality AI, though he is "broadly encouraged" rather than chasing, with SPX December upside volatility back to 13. Brent fell almost 6% as Trump cited progress toward ending the Iran war. Privorotsky calls this "containment, not de-escalation" and stays balanced given how fast the market has repriced. The Senate's bipartisan permitting bill cleared a procedural vote 73-25, which he reads as data centers getting built with more conditions rather than a moratorium, a view Constellation Energy's earnings beat supports. For today's CPI, Goldman forecasts a soft headline (+0.21%) and core (+0.16%) versus consensus, and notes 2-year inflation swaps have dropped 45bps in three weeks even as the NY Fed's consumer survey shows expectations stuck near a 3-year high. On Nvidia, the market compartmentalized Jensen Huang's scandal from AI demand. Privorotsky's unresolved worry is compute oversupply, tested by CoreWeave's earnings today.
